newsitem.title: USA: Revlon holding co 144As top slate, flows up.
newsitem.headline: Revlon holding co 144As top slate, flows up.

text.p: Revlon Worldwide Corp's $500 million 144A zero coupon bonds may capture a yield to maturity through 11 percent when priced on Friday, sources said.

Such a tight pricing would buck street talk on Thursday of an 11-1/8 percent backstop to the deal - suggesting lead manager Chase Securities and Revlon Worldwide may be offering more favorable terms in the indenture, one analyst said.

Meanwhile, dealers noted cash-rich mutual funds have bolstered the long-standing high-yield euphoria. In the last week, funds reported inflows of $526 million compared with $335 million in the previous week, an analyst said.

Back to Revlon, dealers and analysts alike note the Street has been unusually tight-lipped about the details surrounding the deal. The deal was announced one week ago when the company said it would defease $1.15 billion in accrued value of its outstanding zeros due 1998.
Cash for the defeasement will be raised through Friday's offering and an investment by MacAndrews & Forbes Holdings.

One high-yield analyst who declined to be named said investors had been demanding for tighter covenants to the bond deal, which may have included provisions enabling the company to add more debt senior to those notes.
There is also a question as to whether the company will offer registration rights with the deal, the analyst said.
Still, some said a rich price for the new four-year zeros may be palatable given the Street's sanguine outlook for Revlon's equity. Revlon shares are currently trading near their year high at 38-3/8.
Chase Securities' syndicate would not comment.

Other high-yield issuance on Friday included $250 million 10-year nior subordinated notes from Tracor Inc priced to yield 200 basis points over the Treasury curve. The deal was increased by $50 million on Friday.
BT Securities Corp was lead manager on the deal.

Investment grade issues will be led by a $200 million double-tranche deal from MAPCO Inc via joint lead managers J.P. Morgan Securities Inc and Chase Securities. The deal is expected to include $100 million debt due 2009 priced around 73 basis points over the curve and $100 million 30-year debt priced near an 85 basis point spread.
